XCM as both a term and art form was originally pioneered by De'vo vom Schattenreich of Germany.

As I discussed in the first of this series of posts, wandering monsters are something players will want to avoid. Wandering monsters use up resources without awarding much in the way of treasure and hence experience points. Wandering monsters serve to discourage players from searching every square foot of a dungeon for secret doors, from spending multiple turns attempting to bash open a door or pick a lock, or from making really, really sure that a chest is not trapped. In 5e, wandering monsters also serve as an additional consideration when deciding whether it is worth the risk to attempt a short or long rest.

Here is a complete set of old school wandering monster tables. These are modeled after those found in the AD&D Monster Manual II and include tables for dungeon, wilderness, aquatic, and extra-planar adventures. Dungeon tables are scaled to party level using the "easy" to "deadly" XP Encounter Thresholds in the DMG. Wilderness tables are unscaled. This construction reflects a central assumption in old school D&D that players could expect to have some degree of control over risk vs. reward in the dungeon but that no holds are barred in the great outdoors, although civilized areas are somewhat safer than the wilderness.

These tables are similar to those I have posted elsewhere but now include monsters from Fifth Edition Foes. There are also a few monsters from the old Field Folio and Monster Manual II, generally non-combat monsters. Page numbers are given for each entry for convenience. If you do not like the choices I made, here is the LATEX source code. Feel free to change things to suit your own needs.

I roll 1d6 for wandering encounters every two 10-minute turns (more on turns in a later post) in the dungeon; an encounter occurs on a roll of 1. In the wilderness, I roll 1d8 each day and 1d6 each night, and again we have an encounter on a roll of 1. My friends have their own, similar systems. Use what works for you!
